name: CHIMERIC ANTIGEN RECEPTOR T-CELL (CAR-T) THERAPY
indication: CAR-T therapy with Tisacel (Tisagenlecleucel) for the treatment of paediatric and young adult patients up to and including 25 years of age with: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (ALL) that is refractory, in relapse post-transplant or in second or later relapse.

drugs.special_instructions: Dose banded according to national dose bands. Irritant (extravasation risk).
Dose banded according to national dose bands (100mg/ml). Neutral (irritant in large volumes) (extravasation risk).

Overall dose range: 1.2 x 10^6 – 6 x 10^8 cells. Target dose for patients 50kg and below: 0.2 to 5 x 10^6 cells/kg body weight. Target dose for patients above 50kg: 0.1 to 2.5 x 10^8 cells (non-weight based). Administered gravimetrically, not via a volumetric pump. Administer via latex-free giving set without a leukocyte depleting filter and primed with sodium chloride 0.9%. Infusion must be over a maximum of 30 minutes. Gently agitate bag during infusion to prevent cell clumping. If volume ≤20 mL, IV push may be used. Rinse tubing with 10-30ml 0.9% sodium chloride solution after infusion. Administration should not occur out of core hours or over a weekend. Tisacel infusion should be infused within 30 minutes of thaw completion time. The product should be administered immediately after thawing. One individual treatment dose comprises 1 or more infusion bags. Each infusion bag may contain either 10–30 ml (50 ml bag) or 30–50 ml (250 ml bag) cell dispersion. The start and stop time of infusion must be documented, including any interruption. Once completed, the infusion bag(s) and giving set must be disposed of in clinical waste, in accordance with Trust policy.

pre_medications.special_instructions: When required as a premedication. Maximum dose 4000mg/24 hours.

take_home_medicines.special_instructions: Commencing on day 0 until day +30. For weaning: reduce to 250mg orally twice daily for two weeks, then 250mg once daily for one week and then stopped. Considered for seizure prophylaxis due to neurotoxicity risk or history of seizures.
Anti-infective prophylaxis, starting on first day of lymphodepletion (Day -5). Continue until neutrophil recovery.

Anti-infective prophylaxis, starting on first day of lymphodepletion (Day -5). Continue until neutrophil recovery or switch to posaconazole if prolonged neutropenia or prior invasive fungal infection.
Anti-infective prophylaxis. Administered during lymphodepletion, then continued every 28 days until count recovery sufficient for co-trimoxazole use at consultant advice.
Anti-infective prophylaxis: prescribed if prolonged neutropenia or previous invasive fungal infection, starting on first day of lymphodepletion.
To commence on first day of lymphodepletion until platelet count >50 x10^9/L.

Instil 1 drop into each eye four times daily. Start on first day of cytarabine (Day -5). Continue for 5 days after cytarabine administration is complete (last cytarabine Day -4) — total 7 days (Days -5 through +1).

rescue_medications.special_instructions: Can be administered under the supervision of a doctor for the treatment of rigors. PRN only.
Maximum 800mg per dose. Up to four doses, 8-hourly if required, in the event of CRS. Must be prescribed in advance and four doses available on the ward prior to Tisacel infusion.
Four times a day when required for the treatment of fluid overload.
TLS prophylaxis: start on day of lymphodepletion (Day -5) and continue through Day 0. Re-review on day of Tisacel infusion.
TLS prophylaxis: start on day of lymphodepletion (Day -5) and continue through Day 0. Re-review on day of Tisacel infusion (Day 0).

dose_modifications.description: Bilirubin > 34 µmol/L: reduce Cytarabine to 50% of original dose.
If Bilirubin 30-51 µmol/L OR AST 60-180 units/L OR ALT 60-180 units/L: reduce Etoposide to 50% of original dose.
If Bilirubin > 51 µmol/L OR AST > 180 units/L OR ALT > 180 units/L: Clinical decision for Etoposide dose.
If Bilirubin 30-51 µmol/L OR AST 60-180 units/L OR ALT 60-180 units/L: reduce Etoposide to 50% of original dose.

Creatinine Clearance < 60 ml/min: reduce Cytarabine to 60% of original dose.
Creatinine Clearance < 45 ml/min: reduce Cytarabine to 50% of original dose.
Creatinine Clearance < 30 ml/min: Clinical decision for Cytarabine dose modification.
Creatinine Clearance 15-50 ml/min: reduce Etoposide to 75% of original dose.
Creatinine Clearance < 15 ml/min: reduce Etoposide to 50% of original dose.

adverse_effects: oral and anal inflammation or ulceration
neurologic adverse reactions - immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS)

monitoring: FBC, U&Es, renal, liver and bone, CRP, coagulation screen, ferritin and LDH prior to initiating treatment and daily thereafter.
Screening for HBV, HCV and HIV must be performed before collection of cells for Tisagenlecleucel manufacture.
Echocardiogram and baseline measure of lung function must be taken prior to initiating lymphodepletion.
Temperature, blood pressure and oxygen saturation monitored 4-hourly after Tisacel administration on Day 0 and then twice daily as directed in accordance with local procedures.

CRS graded on the WBMT CRS Assessment Form in the patient's notes. Nearly all patients treated with Tisacel experience some degree of CRS, including life-threatening and fatal reactions. CRS symptoms include: pyrexia, tiredness, cardiac failure, tachycardia, cardiac arrhythmias, dyspnoea, hypoxia, capillary leak syndrome, chills, renal impairment, headache, malaise, transaminitis, nausea, diarrhoea, hypotension.

ICE score of the patient must be assessed twice daily and documented on the WBMT ICE Assessment Form in the patient's notes. ICANS symptoms include: seizures, somnolence, headaches, confusion, agitation, speech disorders, tremor, encephalopathy, ataxia, memory impairment, mental status changes, hallucinations, depressed level of consciousness, delirium, dysmetria.
See WBMT Policy P-G-1 and SOP P-P-78 and P-P-79 for monitoring requirements.
warnings: This regimen will only be available to prescribe at the Wessex Blood and Marrow Transplant Unit.
Lymphodepleting chemotherapy must be administered prior to Tisacel.
For autologous use only.

This cytarabine and etoposide lymphodepleting regimen may be considered with Tisacel, in preference to the Tisacel – Fludarabine (30) Cyclophosphamide (500), if the patient has experienced a previous Grade 4 haemorrhagic cystitis with cyclophosphamide, or demonstrated a chemorefractory state to a cyclophosphamide-containing regimen administered shortly before lymphodepleting chemotherapy.
Symptoms of CRS or ICANS can occur weeks after infusion and therefore the patient must be issued with an alert card to carry with them at all times.
Any suspected adverse reaction to a CAR-T cell infusion should be reported via www.mhra.gov.uk/yellowcard.
Consideration should also be given to reporting adverse events to the relevant manufacturer via their usual channels.
Lymphodepleting chemotherapy may be omitted if a patient is experiencing significant cytopenia (e.g., white blood cell (WBC) count ≤1,000 cells/µL) within one week prior to infusion.

Tisacel contains genetically modified (GM) human blood cells. Exposure to Tisacel must be avoided. Procedures for handling, personal protective equipment, spills and waste disposal must be adhered to.
Tisacel cells are cryopreserved in a bag and require thawing prior to administration.
CAR-T administration should not occur out of core hours or over a weekend.
Gently agitate the Tisacel bag during infusion to prevent cell clumping.
If the volume of Tisacel to be administered is ≤20 mL, intravenous push may be used as an alternative method of administration.
All contents of the Tisacel infusion bag(s) should be infused. If more than one infusion bag, the next bag should only be thawed after the contents of the preceding bag have been infused.
Once the full volume of Tisacel has been administered, rinse the tubing at the same rate with 10-30ml 0.9% sodium chloride solution to ensure all Tisacel is delivered.

If the Tisacel bag is not fully administered, this must be documented, and the consultant & pharmacist notified. The manufacturer must be informed and the remaining Tisacel should be discarded in clinical waste, with their approval.
A GM spill-kit must be transported with Tisacel and available on the ward of administration. Local procedures must be followed in the event of a spill.

Local guidelines on handling of waste of human-derived-materials must be followed in case of accidental exposure. Work surfaces and materials which have potentially been in contact with Tisacel must be decontaminated with approved disinfectants.

Prophylactic use of systemic corticosteroids is not recommended as it may interfere with the activity of the cellular therapy and therefore, they should not be administered as part of the pre-medication. However, corticosteroids may be used in the treatment of CRS or ICANS under consultant advice.
Seizure prophylaxis may be considered due to the risk of neurotoxicity associated with Tisacel or if the patient has a history of seizures.
Tocilizumab must be prescribed as when required in advance of CAR-T infusion, in the event of CRS.

Tumour lysis syndrome (TLS) prophylaxis should be prescribed according to the individual patient TLS risk and at consultant review. This must start on the day of lymphodepletion and be re-reviewed on the day of Tisacel infusion.
Where significant reductions in albumin levels occur consider reducing the dose of etoposide.

A minimum period of time must elapse between last dose of conditioning chemotherapy and CAR-T infusion, and a longer period is required for patients with renal insufficiency. This information can be found on the patient's CAR-T cell schedule.
CAUTION: Do not administer Tisacel in patients with unresolved serious adverse reactions (especially pulmonary, cardiac reactions or hypotension) from preceding chemotherapies.
CAUTION: Do not administer Tisacel in patients with active uncontrolled infection or inflammatory disease.
CAUTION: Do not administer Tisacel in patients with active GVHD.
Lymphodepleting regimen must only be started after availability of Tisacel is confirmed.
Ensure patient has been issued with and is carrying the Tisacel treatment alert card prior to discharge. Symptoms of CRS or ICANS can occur weeks after infusion.
Heparin line lock must be managed in accordance with Trust central venous access device management procedure.
See WBMT Policy P-G-1 and SOP P-P-78 and P-P-79 for CRS monitoring requirements and further administration direction.
